subject: FinNext: model scout recommendations & next steps
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Liam Chen <liam.chen@finnext.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-11T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: FinNext discovery — quick post-call recap and proposed trial plan

Liam / Maria — thanks again for a productive 30 minutes today. Quick recap of what we heard and a pragmatic next step so we keep momentum: 

Summary of needs
- Candidate flows: automated underwriting question-answering + customer-support summary generation.
- Throughput: modest (POC) then scale to 500 concurrent sessions.
- Key constraints: PII handling, latency target ~300ms p50 for short answers, and strong quality on domain-specific financial terminology.

Model-scout recommendations (for POC)
- Open model to try first: Mix-13B-FT (we recommend a quantized fp4 variant) — best balance of cost/latency for retrieval-augmented Q&A in our bench.
- Proprietary baseline suggestion: Your current in-house LLM (baseline) or a smaller finetuned LLM — we propose an A/B with the Mix-13B-FT as the challenger.

Acceptance thresholds we suggest for parity
- Accuracy/QA F1: challenger within -5 points of baseline on the provided labeled subset.
- Hallucination rate: no more than 2x baseline on our prompt-set spot checks.
- Latency: p50 within 1.5x of baseline for identical input sizes.

What I attached / links
- Prompt bundle: fnx_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (short labeled prompts + edge cases).
- Benchmark summary (quick scrape): fnx_benchmark_summary_20260311.xlsx and a short dashboard link above.

Proposed next steps (timeline for POC)
1) You share a 1–2k sample (scrubbed) and confirm data handling requirements (end of week).
2) We run a 3-day run with Mix-13B-FT + your baseline, produce benchmark sheet and signal dashboard (week of Mar 16).
3) Sync on verdict and operational recommendations (canary config, batching profile, and quantization) — Mar 19 call.

Ask from you
- Confirm you can provide a scrubbed sample and whether SOC2 / contractual security proof points should be included up front.

If that all looks good I’ll get Prio (cc'd) to run the quick internal checklist (Karthik: notes on infra/quantization below) and open a HubSpot POC record.

Thanks — Avery
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Liam Chen <liam.chen@finnext.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Ortiz <maria.ortiz@finnext.com>
Date: 2026-03-11T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinNext discovery — quick post-call recap and proposed trial plan

Avery — thanks for the crisp notes and suggested thresholds. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Data sample: we can provide a 1,200-row scrubbed CSV by Friday EOD. It will include short QA pairs and support transcripts (no account numbers).
2) Security: SOC2 certs would be great to have up front; we may need an addendum for data retention. Can you send the standard SOC2 + DPA links?
3) SLA / latency: 300ms p50 is reasonable. If the challenger meets quality but is slightly slower, would Redwood recommend batching or a two-tier routing approach?

Also — Maria asked whether Redwood can run prompt-injection tests as part of the POC. If not included, we’ll plan to run our own.

We’d like to proceed with the POC. Please confirm and we’ll share the scrubbed dataset by Friday.

Best,
Liam
Liam Chen
Head of AI, FinNext
liam.chen@finnext.com
+1 (212) 555-0133

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>, Prio Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-11T18:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinNext discovery — quick post-call recap and proposed trial plan

Avery — quick tech notes for the POC so we set expectations internally: 

- Quantization: fp4 gives a solid cost/latency win for Mix-13B-FT; we'll run a short internal perf sweep to pick kernel paths. Prio — can you reserve a small dedicated slot on the test cluster for Mar 15–16?
- Routing: to address their batching question, recommend a two-tier route: low-latency pool (smaller batch, higher cost) for interactive sessions + batch pool for background scoring. We can enable sticky routing by session id.
- Prompt-injection tests: we can include Redwood's standard suite (we have a curated set) — good to run alongside FinNext's tests.
- Data handling: we’ll provide SOC2 summary + DPA link; for retention we can propose 30-day encrypted KV cache with option to disable caching for PII-heavy inputs.

I’ll assemble a short runbook (2–3 pages) for the POC and drop it in the Drive folder. If anyone on infra wants to join the kickoff, loop them in.

Karthik
Sr. Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
